finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, but the result is discarded. Any authenticated user can delete any project (broken authorization). The sibling PUT route correctly uses authorize(), which throws.
finding.source: Any authenticated user sends DELETE /projects/<victim project id>. req.params.id is attacker-controlled.
finding.sink: req.store.projects.delete(project.id) at api.js:19, the protected delete operation.

trace.note: project is loaded by attacker-supplied id with no ownership filter
authorized(req.user, project) returns true or false. The return value is ignored and nothing throws.
authorized() only returns a boolean. It has no throw path, unlike authorize() at line 4.

finding.guards_checked: Checked for authorization middleware in this file and found none. req.user is assumed to be set upstream, and that code is not in this repo. authorized() is the only check on the path, and its result is unused. Nothing else gates the call. A nonexistent id makes project undefined, so line 18 throws a TypeError (500), which is a robustness issue and not a bypass.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 only returns a boolean; its result is discarded at api.js:18. No middleware or other check exists in the repo, which contains only api.js. req.user is assumed to be set upstream.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized(), which returns a boolean (api.js:13) and has no throw path, and the result is discarded, so api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated non-owner. The PUT route at api.js:25 uses the throwing authorize() correctly.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:18 only returns a boolean and its result is discarded; no middleware or other check in the directory.
verdict_facts.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized(), which returns a boolean (api.js:12-14), as a bare statement, so api.js:19 deletes the project unconditionally for any authenticated user, unlike authorize() at api.js:25, which throws.

finding.claim: authorize() lets any user with a truthy isAdmin pass, while authorized() requires isAdmin === true. If isAdmin can be a non-boolean value (for example the string "false" from a header, JWT claim or DB text column), non-admins can rename any project. The impact is conditional on how req.user is populated upstream, which is not in this repo. This is a weaker finding than F1.
finding.source: A user whose isAdmin is a truthy non-boolean value, such as the string "false" or "0", sends PUT /projects/<victim id>/name.
finding.sink: project.name = req.body.name at api.js:26, a write to another user's resource.

trace.note: The check !user.isAdmin treats any truthy value as admin, unlike the strict === true at line 13
The attacker-controlled name is written to the project

finding.guards_checked: The ownerId comparison is correct for the normal case. The strict isAdmin check exists only in the unused authorized() function. The type of req.user.isAdmin could not be verified because the auth middleware is not in this repo. A missing project also throws a TypeError.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at api.js:4-10 throws a 403 when ownerId differs and !user.isAdmin. It is called as a bare statement at api.js:25, which is fine because it throws and nothing catches the error. The strict authorized() at api.js:12-14 is only called, with its result discarded, in the DELETE handler at api.js:18.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate (api.js:5 uses a truthy !user.isAdmin, api.js:25 calls the throwing authorize(), api.js:26 writes the name), but whether req.user.isAdmin can be a truthy non-boolean such as "false" depends on auth middleware that is not in this repo, since api.js is the only file.

verdict_facts.guard_found: authorize() at api.js:5 throws 403 when ownerId !== user.id and !user.isAdmin, and it is called at api.js:25 before the write. The strict authorized() at api.js:13 is only a bare statement at api.js:18 on the delete route, not on the name route.
verdict_facts.reason: The trace is accurate (api.js:5 uses a truthy check, api.js:13 uses ===true, and api.js:26 writes the name), but exploitation needs req.user.isAdmin to be a truthy non-boolean such as "false". That depends on the upstream middleware, which is outside this directory and described as trusted, so the code here cannot settle it.
